School counsellor's note, Class 9, Thursday

Ayesha, 14, was sent to me after her maths teacher found her copying from Keerthana's paper during the unit test. It was two answers, both word for word.

Ayesha spoke quickly and firmly. "Mrs Raman is the strictest teacher in the school. Half the questions weren't even from the chapter. Everyone copies in her tests, I just got caught." She added, twice, "I'm not a cheater. I'm a good student. Ask anyone."

When I asked what she had done in the test, she looked at the window for a long time.

I think she is holding on to the story that she's a good person who was treated unfairly, because the alternative feels unbearable right now. That picture of herself matters to her, which is actually a good starting point.

Next step: I'll meet her again tomorrow, and help her think about how a good student might put right a mistake, including speaking to Mrs Raman herself.

qa.a: Two answers, both word for word.

Monday night

Geography test today. I'm writing this so I remember it properly.

Question 7 and 8 were about soil types, which Sir never even taught properly. He rushed that chapter in one class. So I looked at Tenzin's paper for those two. Just a glance. Two answers out of twenty.

Honestly, it's Sir's fault. He's so strict and he makes papers that are unfair on purpose. Anyone in my place would have done the same. It's not like I'm a cheater. I'm the girl who helps everyone with maths. I've never done anything like this before.

Tenzin didn't see. Nobody saw.

So why do I keep thinking about it?

I'm a good person. The paper was unfair. Those two things are both true.

I think.

— Nirmala
